messages:
jordan_customer: Hey team — hitting a weird failure on the embeddings/rerank flow after a recent client deploy. Some batched requests throw a dim mismatch error intermittently.

alex_support: Sorry you're seeing that, can you paste a repro curl + request IDs? also need full response body and any server request id from the error.

jordan_customer: Putting what I have below. Happens in prod and staging. Request IDs from responses: req_9f3a, req_9f3b, r-0a7c1. When it fails the response is 400 with message: "embedding.dim_mismatch: expected 1536 got 1024" for one item in the batch. Most responses ok.

jordan_customer: Repro curl I used (sanitized keys):

```
curl -v -X POST https://api.redwood-inference.com/v1/embeddings/batch \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-REDACTED" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  --data-binary '@batch_payload.json'
```

jordan_customer: batch_payload.json is an array of text docs and we send batching on the client. I appended a few vectors from an upstream preproc pipeline (they're numeric arrays).

alex_support: Thanks — two quick asks: 1) can you paste the exact failing response body for one of the request ids (req_9f3a or r-0a7c1)? 2) can you confirm whether you set Content-Encoding: gzip or any Transfer-Encoding: chunked headers? we've seen mismatches when gzip+json interplay happens.

jordan_customer: Here's the raw failing response (copied):

```
HTTP/1.1 400 Bad Request
Content-Type: application/json
X-Request-Id: req_9f3a

{ "error": { "type": "embedding.dim_mismatch", "message": "expected 1536 got 1024 on item 7", "item_index": 7, "expected_dim": 1536, "actual_dim": 1024 } }
```

jordan_customer: We do set Content-Encoding: gzip on some clients. But the same code works a lot of the time, so it's intermittent.

maya_engineer: tagging in — this looks like a mixed-model-variant batching issue. Our batcher can coalesce requests routed to model variants; if one request ends up mapped to a 1024-dim variant and others to 1536 it can fail validation. Need logs from the batcher run that include model_variant decisions and the per-item model fingerprint.

sam_ops: ingest-bot logs show an interesting pattern around r-0a7c1:

```
[INGEST] r-0a7c1 batch_start items=16 route_key=emb-v1
[INGEST] r-0a7c1 item7 fingerprint=fp-1024 variant_hint=quant-1024
[INGEST] r-0a7c1 item7 payload_type=vector raw_len=4096
[INGEST] r-0a7c1 batch_prepare assigned_model=emb-v1-1536
[INGEST] r-0a7c1 validation_error embedding.dim_mismatch expected=1536 actual=1024
```

maya_engineer: That fingerprint on item7 is the smoking gun. Need the client payload for the same item (the actual JSON piece) — sometimes a client mistakenly encodes a precomputed vector (1024 floats) into the text input array and the routing heuristics pick the wrong model.

jordan_customer: Copying the JSON piece for item 7 below (from our logs):

```
{ "id": "u-77", "content": [0.12, 0.03, ..., 0.99] /* 1024 floats */ }
```

jordan_customer: Ah — one of our upstream pipelines attaches a precomputed vector for some records. We thought the API would ignore that when using text mode but looks like the presence of a numeric array triggers vectorize path.

alex_support: That explains the mixed fingerprint. Two mitigation paths: 1) client-side: stop sending numeric arrays in the text batch or normalize payload shape so items are homogeneous per request; 2) server-side workaround: we can add a validation fallback that coerces routing by input-type and rejects heterogeneous batches early with a clearer 400. Which do you prefer?

jordan_customer: We'll patch client immediately. For now can you provide a short reproducer so our QA can run it locally (curl + minimal payload)? Want something that toggles one item to be precomputed vector to cause the failure.

devex: Quick reproducer — save two items to payload.json: one plain text doc, one with a numeric array. Curl below:

```
# payload.json
[
  {"id":"a","text":"what is redwood?"},
  {"id":"b","text":"", "vector": [0.1,0.2, ... /* 1024 floats */] }
]

curl -X POST https://api.redwood-inference.com/v1/embeddings/batch \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-REDACTED' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  --data-binary @payload.json
```

devex: Note: use a 1024-length vector for item b. It should reliably flag a dim_mismatch if the default model is 1536.

maya_engineer: Also include a note to set Content-Encoding only if actually gzipping the file. If you use --data-binary with an already gzipped file and send wrong headers you can get parse/shape oddities.

sam_ops: I'll attach the server batcher debug bundle request template. Please run it once with failing case and send back bundle_id from /debug/bundles endpoint. That gives us the full trace (routing decisions, kernel selection, payload checksum).

jordan_customer: Will run reproducer and send bundle_id + failing request ids. ETA 90m. Thanks all :thumbsup:

alex_support: Perfect — once you paste bundle_id + req ids we'll escalate to a patch if we see consistent mixed routing. Meanwhile we can add a guard to return early with clearer error.

jordan_customer: bundle created: bndl-44c2, recorded reqs: req_9f3a, r-0a7c1. Sent to support inbox.

maya_engineer: Got the bundle. We can reproduce locally and will push a short validation patch to fail fast on heterogeneous batches. Will follow up with a patch PR and can coordinate a canary rollout.

alex_support: Great, closing loop once PR is live. If you need an emergency mitigation we can add a per-tenant block for mixed-shape batches until client patch is rolled.

jordan_customer: Appreciate it, will remove vector attach from client and retest.

ingest-bot: automated note: bundle bndl-44c2 processed, linked traces: t-8811, t-8812.

maya_engineer: updating internal ticket with root cause: upstream client attaching precomputed vectors -> mixed-shape batch -> routing to mixed model variants -> dim mismatch. Patch & canary scheduled.

alex_support: Thanks everyone. If anything changes ping #support or DM.
